attempted_implications: A is explicitly distinct from B and B is identified with C, but no conclusion is drawn about A versus C.
An UNKNOWN quantifier makes the whole existential-typing check indeterminate even when another occurrence is definitively FORALL or a free parameter.
exact_failures: Distinctness was queried only on direct occurrence pairs, so equivalence closure could hide a conclusive inequality.
An elif made uncertainty mask a separately known non-existential obstruction.
falsifiers: A countermodel where A != B and B = C but A = C.
A valid joint existential witness whose required occurrence is universally quantified or only a free parameter under the frozen contract.
proof_evidence: Substitutivity of equality: B=C and A!=B imply A!=C.
Conjunctive obligation typing: every required occurrence must satisfy EXISTS; a single FORALL/FREE_PARAMETER violates the contract.
repairs: Project explicit distinct relations to final DSU roots, reject any distinct relation internal to one root, and query distinct root pairs for every joint obligation.
Evaluate UNKNOWN and known non-existential quantifiers independently, then give deterministic failure precedence over cannot-check.
scope: Proposal-shadow co-witness routing decisions after SAME_WITNESS, alpha-renaming, and binder-id closure.
supported_causes: Identity is an equivalence relation, so disequality must be represented between equivalence classes rather than raw occurrence pairs.
For a joint existential obligation, all listed occurrences must be existential; one known non-existential occurrence is a decisive falsifier independent of other unknowns.
